sections.title: About the role:
paras: Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory company accelerating the abundance of energy and intelligence through modular infrastructure. We are seeking a Principal Hardware Product Manager to own the multi-year Hardware roadmap and Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) for Crusoe Spark™, our modular datacenter.

In this role, “hardware” and “product” refers to the physical infrastructure of the Spark module: structural steel modules, RPPs, DLC cooling loops, CDUs, chillers, piping headers, electrical and mechanical systems, and power distribution gear. Compute hardware (servers, GPUs, storage, networking, and rack specifications) is owned by Cloud Product. Cloud Product defines the compute needs; you define the Hardware that houses and powers it.

sections.title: What You'll Be Working On:
paras: I. Physical Module Roadmap & Design Requirements
II. Requirements Ownership & Engineering Partnership
bullets: Hardware Roadmap Ownership: Own and maintain the multi-year Spark hardware roadmap.
Hardware PRD Authorship: Author precise Spark PRDs for physical modules, translating compute needs into concrete structural, thermal, and electrical specifications.

Physical Version Management: Manage hardware generation transitions. Define cut-in criteria, retrofit rules, module-side accommodation of rack footprint, loading, and cooling interface per Cloud Product’s rack specifications., and documentation required for manufacturing release.

Spark Hardware TPM Alignment: Work in lockstep with Spark Hardware TPMs and engineering discipline leads (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, Thermal) to guide physical development from concept to build.

Requirements Discipline: Set clear product hardware requirements (module power distribution capacity, thermal capacity, transportability) and hold hardware engineering teams accountable without prescribing detailed sub-component implementation.
Design Partner Leadership: Serve as the primary design contact for external architecture, engineering, and modular design firms.

Requirements intake from Cloud Product: Collaborate with Cloud Product teams to ensure that the physical Spark module hardware supports the GPU & rack-level architecture needs. ashby:mindrobotics:a2861512-d8a8-45f5-bb.summary: Mind Robotics is building Physical AI for real-world industrial deployment, starting with the factory floor. We believe the hardest problems in AI are solved when researchers and engineers are hands-on with the physical world every day - and we're looking for people who are passionate about robotics, value ownership, and are excited to tackle difficult problems. sections.title: About the team and the role:
paras: Teleoperation is how Mind Robotics turns human skill into robot capability. Every hour an operator spends guiding one of our humanoids through a real factory task becomes training data for our models. As our robots go into production, teleoperation is also how a person steps in remotely when a robot needs help. This role productizes that capability.

You own the full teleoperation system: the operator rig and interface, the software and network stack that connects an operator to a robot, the operator workforce program, and the data that flows out the other end into our research platform. You report directly to Daniel Burrows, Head of Data.

This is not a role where you inherit a roadmap and manage a backlog. You'll define what teleoperation at Mind becomes: how many robot-hours of high-quality demonstrations we can produce per week, at what cost, across how many tasks and sites. You'll work across research, robotics hardware, controls, software, data infrastructure and operations. You'll spend real time in the teleop room and on factory floors with the operators, researchers, and site teams who use what we build.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
paras: The product scope will evolve, but here's the kind of work you'll own:
bullets: Product strategy and roadmap. Define the roadmap for the full teleoperation stack: operator hardware (VR headsets, leader arms, gloves and hand tracking), the operator interface, robot-side control and safety, networking and latency, and the pipeline that delivers episodes to our training data.

Throughput, quality, and cost. Own the metrics that matter: usable episodes per operator-hour, task success rate, data quality against research specs, and cost per usable hour. Then build the product to move them, and give the Data team clear in-house numbers to compare against external vendors.

Operator experience and workforce programs. Treat operators as your primary users. Design the recruiting profile, training and certification path, QA feedback loops, shift structure, and ergonomics that let operators produce consistent, high-quality data without burning out.

Research partnership. Work with the Teleops Program team and Research to turn what the models need (new tasks, embodiments, environments, failure-recovery demonstrations, annotations) into collection plans and product requirements, and close the loop when data quality issues show up downstream.

Remote operations at customer sites. Define how teleoperation supports robots deployed in factories: remote assistance and intervention, the handoff between autonomy and a human, site networking and IT requirements, and the safety and operating procedures customers will need to approve.
Cross-functional execution. Work with hardware, controls, software, and data infrastructure teams to ship on schedule, then roll out the supporting SOPs to the teleop floor and to customer sites.
Platform expansion. Design the system so adding the next operator station, robot, task, or site is faster than the last. Repeatable deployment, not a custom integration every time.

sections.title: Requirements:
bullets: 8+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a product that combines hardware, software, and an operational workforce, and that several other teams depended on.

You've shipped robotics, AR/VR, autonomy, or other real-time hardware-software systems. You understand latency budgets, sensor and network constraints, and what happens when a system meets the physical world.

Technical depth across the stack. You don't write the control code, but you know the difference between hard, impossible, and untried, and you can hold your own in a technical review with controls and ML engineers.
You've run or partnered closely with an operations team: hiring, training, QA, and the metrics that tell you whether people and process are working.

Strong written communication. You can turn complex tradeoffs between throughput, data quality, cost, and operator experience into clear decisions for leadership, and state product priorities to an engineering team without hedging.
You've worked on teleoperation, robot learning data collection, or remote operations for autonomous vehicles or robots.
You think about operator experience the way a consumer PM thinks about users, and about data quality the way an ML researcher does, and you don't treat them as separate problems.
You're comfortable with numbers. You'll build the model for cost per usable hour yourself and use it to argue for where the next dollar goes.

ashby:spare:c637c751-4cf0-4822-9426-733d.summary:

The Enterprise segment is a finite market . There are roughly 150 large transit agencies in North America that qualify as Enterprise for us, and we already serve a meaningful share of them. That single fact reshapes what account management means here. We cannot grow this segment by adding logos at volume — the growth has to come from going deeper into agencies we already serve, defending contracts that come up for re-procurement, and attaching products beyond the one that got us in the door.

sections.title: Why this role exists
paras: That is the job. You will own the commercial outcome of Spare's existing Enterprise relationships: net revenue retention, gross retention, multi-product expansion, and renewal defense against well-funded competitors who want our installed base.

This is not a customer success role wearing a commercial hat. This is a Sales Leadership role . You will carry a number, build a team that carries numbers, and be accountable for a material share of Spare's revenue plan.

sections.title: What you'll own
paras: The Enterprise installed base. Roughly 60–70 agency customers today, spanning our largest strategic accounts (multi-million-dollar contracts, multi-year procurement cycles, national reference value) through to newer Enterprise logos with significant untapped platform potential.
A team of Enterprise Account Managers. You will inherit and grow a small, senior team.

sections.title: A revenue number with three components:
paras: The renewal and re-procurement calendar. In public sector, a renewal is frequently a new competitive procurement. Knowing which of our contracts expire when, which will go to open RFP, which can be extended or modified, and what has to be true 18 months out to survive that event — that visibility is your responsibility to build and maintain.
bullets: Expansion ARR: Cross-sell and upsell into the installed base — Fixed Route, AI Voice, EAM, and Demand Response scope growth
Gross retention: Contract renewals and re-procurements held, including competitive recompetes
Multi-product attach rate: Percentage of Enterprise accounts running more than one Spare product

Align expansion timing to how public agencies actually buy — fiscal year budget development, capital planning cycles, and federal and state funding programs (5307, 5310, 5311, CMAQ, state SGR pools)
Partner with Solutions Engineering on technical discovery and workflow design for expansion scope; partner with Marketing and Product Marketing on product-specific enablement

ashby:speak:bc7e4ce2-af3c-423c-ab61-587b.summary:
Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders…

sections.title: About this role
paras: Speak is building an AI tutor that remembers useful context across lessons, responds naturally to learner speech, and adapts what it teaches. Making this work reliably across languages and proficiency levels requires more than one model: it depends on voice technology, learner memory, generated content, evaluation, and the systems that put them together.

We're hiring a Product Lead for Learning Technology to own product direction across these capabilities. You'll work directly with our founders, engineering and research leaders, and the teams building Speak's Tutor to decide where to use external models, improve existing systems, or develop technology of our own — and which investments will actually improve the learner experience.

This is a hands-on product leadership role. You'll build and lead PMs across Voice ML, AI Platform, Content Quality, and Memory while remaining involved in the most important technical product decisions. Initially, you'll take direct responsibility for priority areas that lack dedicated PM ownership, particularly shared AI systems and evaluations.

sections.title: What you'll be doing
bullets: Own Learning Technology product direction and investment choices across voice, AI platform and evaluations, learner memory, and generated-content quality.
Work with Core Learning to identify which changes in model behavior, lesson quality, personalization, or real-time interaction would most improve Tutor use and learning.
Decide when to adopt a new model, fine-tune one, build a specialized capability, or use an external service, weighing quality, latency, reliability, and cost.

Shape evaluation and release decisions for learner speech and real-time voice, including ASR, TTS, and new conversational models. Connect model benchmarks to performance in actual lessons and conversations.
Set product requirements for the Tutor agent harness, model-serving and shared AI tooling, prioritizing the reliability and capabilities product teams need over unnecessary platform work.

Work with Content Quality and Learning Design to improve generated lessons, curriculum inputs, and content evaluations. Keep teaching standards and learner-facing teaching decisions with the teams that own them.
Take promising research and prototypes through integration, production measurement, and iteration; make the build, buy, extend, or stop decision when evidence arrives.
Hire, coach, and manage PMs who can independently own technical product areas and make consequential decisions without routing everything through you.

Those platforms were built for a slower era, with manual setup, fragmented workflows, and insights that arrive too late to shape decisions. The gap between how fast businesses move and how fast research can keep up has never been wider.

We're building something different. With Sprig, AI agents design studies, adapt surveys in real time, and turn responses into clear insight. Research, insights, and customer experience teams move from question to evidence in hours instead of weeks, without sacrificing rigor.

ashby:supabase:a9ad80ae-4514-41c0-8062-3.summary: Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to own Postgres itself at Supabase. Every Supabase project is a full Postgres database, and Postgres is the foundation that Auth, Storage, Realtime and Edge Functions run on. You'll own the product experience of the database: Postgres versions and upgrades, maintenance, observability, extensions and security.

You'll work closely with our Postgres engineering teams and with the PM lead for Databases, who leads Multigres . You'll define the Postgres requirements that architecture must meet, and own how customers experience their database through that transition.

This role is ideal for someone who loves Postgres, sweats the details that make a database trustworthy, and is excited about improving the experience for millions of developers. Small improvements here compound across every project on the platform.

sections.title: What You’ll Be Responsible For
bullets: You'll own Postgres versions, upgrades and end-of-life. Which major and minor versions we support, how and when customers upgrade, and how we retire old versions. Your goal is to make upgrades routine rather than risky.
You'll make maintenance predictable. You'll design how we schedule, communicate and run maintenance windows so customers stay informed and in control, and disruption is rare and expected.
You'll help developers understand their database. Query performance, metrics, logs and advisors: you'll own the path from "my database is slow" to the fix.
You'll own our extension ecosystem. Which extensions we offer, how we evaluate and support new ones, and how we keep them working across versions.
You'll own Postgres security. Roles and permissions, Row Level Security ergonomics, secure defaults, and how we respond to Postgres and extension CVEs.
You'll talk to developers across the full spectrum , from indie developers on their first project to enterprises running critical workloads, and bring what you learn into every prioritization call.

You'll own the problem definition, requirements and success metrics for what we ship, such as upgrade success rate, the share of the fleet on supported versions, and time-to-diagnose for performance problems. You'll set the metric before the team builds, then track it after launch.
You'll keep Engineering, Support and GTM aligned. You'll own the plan of record for what's coming, why, and in what order, and communicate version changes and deprecations clearly to customers.

sections.title: Must have
bullets: 4+ years of Product Management experience on databases, developer tools or infrastructure , or equivalent depth as an engineer, DBA or founder moving into product. You're comfortable commenting on an architecture doc and advocating for the user when trade-offs are required.
Know Postgres well , or another relational database well enough to ramp quickly. You're comfortable reading EXPLAIN output and talking about replication, WAL, roles and extensions.
Have shipped products where reliability and trust are the experience. You treat downtime and breaking changes as product problems, not just operational ones.
Write clearly. Your specs, announcements and deprecation notices leave little room for confusion.
Build with what you own. You run queries, test upgrades and try extensions yourself, and form opinions through first-hand use.
Use AI to move faster. You use AI tools to compress research, drafting and feedback synthesis so you spend more time on judgment calls.
Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

sections.title: Strong signal
bullets: Worked on a managed database service.
Ran Postgres in production: upgrades, tuning, incident response.
Worked on database observability, performance tooling, or security and compliance products.
Contributed to Postgres, its extensions, or the wider open-source community.
Shipped something using Supabase.

Every business in America needs a bank account to exist. The system that decides whether they're real, who's behind them, and whether they're a risk, runs on infrastructure from the 1980s. We're rebuilding that layer from scratch.

Baselayer is the identity layer for institutions across the United States — the most complete business graph in America and every human tied to it. We fuse public records, IRS data, sanctions lists, web signals, and fraud telemetry from 2,200+ financial institutions into a single graph that resolves any business and the humans behind it in milliseconds. The legacy credit bureaus took 50 years to build something that gets 60% match rates. We've built something that gets 98% in under two years.

sections.title: ABOUT BASELAYER
paras: Today we're trusted by over 20% of financial institutions in America — including FIS, Rho, Socure and leading loan infrastructure providers. But the graph is becoming infrastructure for anyone who needs to know if a business is real and worth trusting: gig platforms, marketplaces, AI companies, and commerce infrastructure at scale.
Trust is the substrate of every financial transaction. We're rebuilding it.

sections.title: ABOUT THE TEAM
paras: We're solving real-time entity resolution at a scale no one else has cracked — fusing dozens of data sources into a single business identity graph and resolving any entity in milliseconds. It's a graph AI problem, a retrieval problem, and a fraud-modeling problem stacked on top of each other. The technical depth is real.

You'd be joining a small team where the data moat is defensible, the research problems are open, and the infrastructure you build becomes load-bearing for businesses. Ownership is real. Velocity is real. There's no layer of process between an idea and shipping it.

We're at an inflection point — the graph is built, the match rates speak for themselves, and the hardest problems are still ahead: graph embeddings, fraud propagation models across the business network, real-time traversal at sub-100ms latency, and expanding the identity layer beyond finance into every platform that needs to trust a business.

sections.title: ABOUT THE ROLE
paras: As Baselayer's first dedicated Sr. Product Manager, you'll report directly to our CTO and own the creation, design, and full scoping of new products that take Baselayer beyond financial institutions and into new verticals where business identity is broken. This role is hands-on. You'll write the specs, draw the wireframes, partner with design, and sit in eng standups. You'll also own the existing product surface: setting priorities, sequencing the roadmap, and making the daily calls that keep engineering shipping the right things. Outgoing and personable, with each customer, you conduct yourself professionally in both demeanor and presence. You find ways to say yes and put patient and customer experience above all else. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to grow where you want to go, building valuable experience and paving the way for your career to take unexpected and rewarding directions.

sections.title: WHAT YOU’LL DO
bullets: Greet every customer with warmth and urgency, whether in person, over the phone, or online
Oversee all customer communications (calls, emails, texts), record details accurately, and route urgent medical calls to a doctor quickly
Deliver personalized, memorable experiences—always looking for creative ways to say “yes” to customer needs
Listen with empathy, resolve concerns quickly, and anticipate issues before they escalate
Keep nursing team and doctors updated on customer needs for a seamless care experience.
Provide confidential, compassionate guidance on financial options and end-of-life decisions
Process payments accurately while protecting personal and financial information
Follow up with customers after visits to check on their pet’s care and strengthen relationships

sections.title: WHAT YOU NEED
bullets: 2+ years of experience in a customer service role
Advanced knowledge in computer programs and practice management software
Highly organized, with strong attention to detail
A strong communicator; able to interact positively with anyone and everyone
A strong multitasker, able to thrive amid chaos
High emotional intelligence, able to read a room and plan and act accordingly
Adaptable and amenable in high stakes environments
Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

greenhouse:veterinaryemergencygroupst:62.summary:

Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.
VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

VetEvolve is a network of veterinary practices built to support the people delivering care and the practices they lead. We combine clinical insight with operational strength to give our teams the support, tools, and structure they need to thrive, without losing what makes each practice unique. We are intentionally focused on growth, not as an end in itself, but as a way to strengthen our practices, expand access to care, and create more opportunities for our teams.

sections.title: Client Service Representative
paras: Compensation: $18-20 hour, commensurate with experience

The Client Service Representative (CSR) plays a vital role in creating a positive first and lasting impression for our clients and their pets. The CSR is responsible for delivering exceptional service both in person and over the phone, handling client interactions with professionalism, empathy, and care. This position supports the smooth operation of the hospital by managing client communications, maintaining accurate records, and assisting the veterinary team in providing outstanding patient care.
bullets: Greet clients and patients warmly, providing professional, empathetic, and attentive service while answering in-person inquiries promptly.
Complete patient check-in and check-out efficiently while serving as a liaison with hospital staff and communicating real-time patient status and flow changes.
Maintain client communications via phone, email, and mail, including follow-ups and thank-you messages.
Schedule, confirm, and forward book appointments, routing requests appropriately; triage patients based on urgency.
Communicate clearly about hospital services, wellness care, vaccinations, diagnostics, surgical aftercare, and specialty packages.
Handle sensitive situations (e.g., euthanasia, test results, payments) with tact and professionalism.
Maintain accurate patient records, request and attach prior records, and ensure charges are captured.
Complete cash reconciliation, end-of-day financial tasks, and bank deposits while accurately processing payments and refunds, including transactions through Care Credit and credit card terminals.

At Wasabi, we’re a proven collection of pioneers, visionaries and disruptive doers. We see things differently than our competitors, and we make our mark in the industry by challenging the norm and delivering the unexpected and improbable. We’re a fast-growing company taking the Cloud Storage industry by storm and recognized as one of the best places to work in Boston.

Wasabi hot cloud storage is a new class and category of cloud storage, breaking all traditional barriers and boundaries of storage with a disruptive value proposition of being 1/5th the cost of AWS S3, faster than the competition, with no fees for egress or API requests. sections.title: Role Purpose:
paras: AI infrastructure is one of the fastest-growing areas of our business, and we're looking for a senior alliance leader to build our partner strategy across it from the ground up. This is a hunter's role as much as a strategist's: you'll spend real time identifying and pursuing prospective partners who don't yet know Wasabi, as we ll as managing relationships that already exist. The mandate spans three connected areas: AI infrastructure partnerships, AI data factory partnerships (the storage and data layer powering AI training and inference), and the emerging AI developer ecosystem.

This role calls for an AI industry veteran who already has credibility in the AI infrastructure and storage industry — with a network of relationships . You'll own the strategy, and the go-to-market for this motion end to end: evaluating who we partner with, originating those relationships yourself, structuring how the partnership creates revenue, and representing Wasabi commercially and technically with the companies building the AI infrastructure stack. You'll work in close partnership cross functionally with product teams and with our Business Development team to evaluate and pursue neocloud providers, and other AI-native companies as the landscape evolves.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Hunt and originate new partnerships. Proactively identify, prospect, and land new AI infrastructure, data factory, and developer partners — this role is measured on new relationships built, not just existing ones maintained.
Set the partner strategy. Define which AI infrastructure, data factory, and developer partnerships matter most, and build the roadmap to get there.
Drive go-to-market. Build joint GTM plans and co-sell motions that turn partner capabilities into real, trackable revenue.

Partner with Business Development. Work hand-in-hand with BD to identify, evaluate, and develop relationships with OEM partners, neocloud providers, and other emerging AI companies — helping shape deal structure and unlock joint opportunity.
Own the commercial relationship. Lead forecasting, executive alignment, and business reviews for signed partners, from first conversation through signed deal and beyond.
Build the developer ecosystem presence. Establish Wasabi's footprint with AI developer platforms and communities largely from scratch.
Enable the field. Partner with Marketing and Enablement to turn partner strategy into campaigns, positioning, and seller-facing content.
Measure what matters. Track partner performance on new partnerships originated, pipeline, revenue, and engagement — not just activity.

You will set the vision and roadmap for a modular, scalable, multi-tenant gateway that connects Versapay’s accounts receivable products to processors, acquirers, and card & bank network s . You own both the product and business outcomes for the gateways; authorization and payment success rates, uptime and latency, downgrades, cost per transaction, and more .

sections.title: Your Impact at Versapay :
paras: This is a platform role . Your customers are Versapay’s product teams, our core processing partners, the developers and ERP partners who integrate with us, and the ledger and finance teams who depend on every payment landing correctly. You will partner directly with engineering on architecture and delivery, work with go-to-market teams on positioning and regularly represent gateway strategy and performance to senior leadership, influencing direction and investment.
This is an opportunity for a product leader who has built / scaled a payment gateway and is ready to grow and modernize a global B2B payments platform.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Own the gateway strategy and roadmap. Set the multi-year vision for Versapay’s owned gateways across card, bank, and alternative payment methods in every market we serve. Balance near-term improvements with long-term platform investments and make the trade-offs explicit.

Drive payment performance. Own the gateway’s core KPIs: authorization and payment success rates, decline and retry performance, uptime, latency, and processing cost. Improve them through connection optimization, failover, smart retries, network tokenization, account updater, 3DS and authentication flows, and B2B card data (Level 2/3).

Build the platform others build on. Define the gateway’s APIs, SDKs, hosted payment pages, webhooks, and merchant and MID configuration so Versapay product teams and partners can launch new payment experiences in days, not quarters.

Own processor, acquirer, and network connectivity. Lead the evaluation, certification, and launch of processor and acquirer integrations and new network capabilities. Translate network specs and mandates into clear requirements, and keep the gateway compliant with card brand rules, PCI DSS, and regional regulations.

Own the transaction lifecycle end to end. Authorization, capture, refunds, voids, disputes and chargebacks, and settlement, including the clean handoff of transaction data to ledger and reconciliation. Partner with risk, compliance, and payment operations to keep money moving safely.

Lead engineering teams to deliver. Lead engineering team(s) and oversee execution across pods, from writing requirements to measuring success. Drive trade-off decisions on architecture, reliability, and platform design while keeping the team unblocked and managing the SDLC.

Use AI to compound platform value. Apply ML and agentic approaches to retry optimization, decline analysis, anomaly detection, incident triage, and partner integration support. Versapay is rebuilding for an AI-native operating model, and the gateway is core to that.

Be the in-house expert. Serve as Versapay’s authority on gateway architecture, payment processing, and network rules. Educate product and engineering teams, brief executives, and represent the platform externally with partners and customers.

sections.title: What You Bring to the Team:
bullets: 6+ years in payments or fintech product management, with at least 3 years owning a payment gateway, processing, orchestration, or PSP platform end to end. Senior IC who has driven a roadmap, not just contributed to one.
Built or significantly scaled a gateway. You have shipped gateway capabilities in production — not just integrated a third-party gateway — and can speak to what changed and why.

Deep transaction lifecycle expertise. You understand authorization flows, network messaging (ISO 8583), tokenization, capture and settlement, chargebacks, interchange, and failover, and how each affects merchants and cost.
A record of moving payment performance metrics. You have measurably improved authorization rates, processing cost, uptime, or latency, and can show the data.

Global payments expertise. Experience across North America and international markets, including multi-currency processing, local payment methods, and the regimes that govern them (PCI DSS, PSD2/SCA, card brand rules).

Track record of leading engineering teams in execution. You have overseen engineering pods or squads as the product owner, setting priorities, removing blockers, making architectural trade-offs alongside engineering leadership, and shipping on commitment.
AI fluency. Hands-on experience applying LLMs, ML, or agentic systems to payment workflows. You have a clear, defensible point of view on where AI belongs in a gateway and where it must not.
